titulo: Command → output: check the criterion and the /goal evaluator
lead: A criterion only counts if an outsider can check it without trusting the agent. In this lesson you run each criterion of goal.md as a command, see which one passes by shortcut, and learn where the proof has to show up: the /goal evaluator in Claude Code only reads the conversation.
objetivo: check each criterion of goal.md by command, see which level 2 one passes by shortcut, and put the proof in the conversation the /goal evaluator reads.

aprende.t: The command → output format and the three kinds of expected output
conferir-goal.py: OK or FALHOU per criterion, with exit code
A criterion with no command and a criterion that passes by shortcut
What the /goal evaluator sees, and what it doesn't

hero_alt: An analog gauge at maximum next to a thermal printer spitting out a paper tape.

secoes.titulo: From the criterion to the proof in the conversation

nos.detalhe: Each line of goal.md has a command in backticks and the expected output in backticks: a literal snippet, empty, or code N. How to write goal.md (the three layers and the lock) is lesson 2 of course 2; here it is how to check.

Runs each command, compares it with the expected output (whole word: "3 passed" does not match "13 passed") and prints OK or FALHOU with what came back. A criterion with no command counts as FALHOU: it can't be checked.

"pytest exits with code 0" can be gamed: with every test skipped, pytest exits 0. The rehearsal shows this criterion passing as OK while "3 passed" gives FALHOU. The full scale (0 to 4) is lesson 6 of course 0.
The agent runs conferir-goal.py and pastes the whole output. The last line is PRONTO or FALTAM N.

According to the Claude Code documentation, after each turn a small, fast model judges the condition: not met, met, or impossible. It doesn't run commands or read files. If the proof isn't printed in the conversation, it doesn't exist for it.

secoes.volta: FALTAM N: the agent keeps going on the next turn
secoes.legenda: A command you run and the output that shows up: it's the same proof for you, for the headless loop and for the /goal evaluator.

secoes.sub: Six criteria. One has no command and one passes through a shortcut. Find both before you run it.

blocos.rot: kit/goal-ensaio.md (criteria; translation for reading; the file in the kit is in Portuguese)
blocos.conteudo:
## Done criteria
**Function**
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest -q tests/` → `3 passed`
- [ ] `python3 -c "from slug import slug; print(slug('Ação & Reação!'))"` → `acao-reacao`

**Regression**
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest -q tests/ -rs` → `código 0`

**Limit**
- [ ] `git diff --stat HEAD -- tests/ pytest.ini` → `vazio`
- [ ] `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- '*conftest.py' tests/` → `vazio`
- [ ] the code stays clean and well documented

K=~/projetos/loop-r-eng-verificacao-v72/kit
bash $K/ensaio.sh > /dev/null && cd /tmp/ensaio-verif/proj
cp $K/goal-ensaio.md ../goal.md            # outside the project: the agent doesn't edit the criterion

python3 $K/conferir-goal.py ../goal.md; echo "saída: $?"     # A) before the work: it has to fail

$K/agente-falso.sh conftest < /dev/null                       # B) shortcut: skips the tests
python3 $K/conferir-goal.py ../goal.md; echo "saída: $?"

rm conftest.py && $K/agente-falso.sh bom < /dev/null           # C) the right work
sed -i '/limpo e bem documentado/d' ../goal.md                 #    and the criterion with no command goes away
python3 $K/conferir-goal.py ../goal.md; echo "saída: $?"

The command appears cut off at 60 characters in the output. In round B, código 0 gave OK with all three tests skipped: it's the level 2 criterion in goal.md.

abas.rot: Common mistake: a criterion that never fails
abas.html: If round A (before any work) already gives OK on a function criterion, the criterion doesn't measure the work. Every function criterion has to fail beforehand; limit criteria (nothing touched) can pass from the start.

secoes.sub: Because the evaluator only reads the conversation, the condition requires the pasted output. In the goal prompts of the execucao-longa kit and the 15 commands kit, the pattern is the same.

blocos.conteudo: /goal The output of `python3 ~/projetos/loop-r-eng-verificacao-v72/kit/conferir-goal.py <caminho>/goal.md` is pasted in full in this conversation and ends with PRONTO; no file in tests/ or conftest.py was changed; stop after 15 turns and say what was missing.

exercicios.texto: Run a small task with /goal using the condition from the block above, pointing to your goal.md.

perguntas.p: What can the /goal evaluator in Claude Code do to judge the condition?
perguntas.explica: The documentation says it doesn't run commands or read files. The proof has to be printed in the conversation; that's why the condition asks for the pasted output.

perguntas.p: In the rehearsal, with all tests skipped, which criterion passed by mistake?
perguntas.explica: pytest exits with 0 when all tests are skipped. "exit code 0" is level 2 (gameable); "3 passed" as a whole word is not.

perguntas.p: Which of these final messages lets the /goal evaluator decide based on proof?
opcoes: The one that pastes the output of conferir-goal.py ending in PRONTO
The one that asks the user to check the criteria one by one
The one that lists the changed files and summarizes each change made
perguntas.explica: Only the pasted output puts what the command actually printed into the conversation. "Everything went fine" is a report.

perguntas.p: A function criterion passes before any work is done. What does that tell you?
opcoes: That the work is easy and was almost done already
That conferir-goal.py has a bug in reading the output
That the criterion misses the work; rewrite it
perguntas.explica: A function criterion has to fail first. If it already passes, it can't tell done from not done.

itens.texto: A criterion with no command can't be checked; conferir-goal.py counts it as FALHOU.
A function criterion that already passes before the work measures nothing; "exit code 0" alone passes with everything skipped.
The /goal evaluator only reads the conversation: the condition requires the pasted output ending in PRONTO.
